items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: It’s called Early Jazz, A Concise Introduction from its Beginning Through 1929 by Fumi Tomita

ctx.x: Oh definitely no. I think to them, I don’t think they necessarily thought of it as art as such, but it was an art you know. It was, because it involved a high degree and a high level of creativity. The thing that struck me about these musicians that I played with is how different they all sounded live. If they played an arpeggio, even if they played the same thing, if they played [plays clarinet] – if they all played that it would all sound different. And it was different tonal qualities, there were different…
It’s called Early Jazz, A Concise Introduction from its Beginning Through 1929 by Fumi Tomita, who is at University of Massachusetts Amherst.
